content.value_statement: Organizations often lack a structured path from raw data to a compliant, priced offering. This skill coordinates product design, pricing, matching, and trusted delivery.
actual_capabilities: Assesses data resources, buyer scenarios, and product potential.
Structures validation gates from product concept through seed-customer testing.
Develops cost, value, and market-based pricing approaches.
Plans marketplace entry, buyer matching, negotiation, and transaction documentation.
Outlines trusted data-space options for sensitive data collaboration.
limitations: Does not replace legal, regulatory, security, or accredited valuation advice.
Cannot guarantee marketplace listing, buyer interest, pricing, or transaction completion.
Depends on accurate data inventories, buyer evidence, costs, and jurisdiction details.
Provides planning guidance but does not execute transactions or deploy infrastructure.

use_cases.title: Design a Sellable Data Product
use_cases.description: Turn an internal dataset into a validated product concept, buyer profile, and delivery plan.

use_cases.title: Prepare a Defensible Price
use_cases.description: Build a pricing range using costs, buyer value, market comparisons, and negotiation limits.

use_cases.title: Plan Sensitive Data Collaboration
use_cases.description: Assess trusted data-space models, participation rules, and technical controls for restricted data use.

prompt_templates.title: Assess Product Potential
prompt_templates.prompt: Assess whether our dataset can become a data product. Identify buyer scenarios, required evidence, key risks, and the next validation step.
prompt_templates.scenario: Begin with a structured review of one dataset.

prompt_templates.title: Create a Product Plan
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a staged data product plan for [dataset]. Include target buyers, value hypothesis, MVP, seed-customer validation, deliverables, and decision gates.
prompt_templates.scenario: Move from an initial idea to a validated offering.

prompt_templates.title: Develop Pricing and Negotiation
prompt_templates.prompt: Develop pricing for [product]. Compare cost, value, and market methods, then propose anchor, target, and minimum positions with stated assumptions.

prompt_templates.title: Design an End-to-End Transaction
prompt_templates.prompt: Design an end-to-end transaction for [product and jurisdiction]. Cover compliance gates, marketplace route, matching, contract terms, delivery controls, and evidence records.
prompt_templates.scenario: Coordinate advanced product, commercial, governance, and infrastructure decisions.

output_examples.input: We have logistics telemetry and want to sell congestion insights.
output_examples.output: A product brief defining buyer segments, aggregated outputs, validation interviews, privacy controls, and criteria for entering pricing.

output_examples.input: Price a monthly retail footfall benchmark for regional chains.
output: Cost floor based on preparation, quality assurance, delivery, and support.
Value range linked to planning savings and avoided research expense.
Market comparison with anchor, target, and minimum negotiation positions.

output_examples.input: Partners need analysis of sensitive records without receiving raw data.
output_examples.output: A trusted data-space outline covering participant roles, authorization, permitted use, technical options, audit evidence, and operating responsibilities.

best_practices: Validate buyer demand before detailed pricing or marketplace preparation.
State evidence, assumptions, jurisdiction, and pricing basis in every recommendation.
Use compliance and security gates before sharing sensitive or regulated data.
anti_patterns: Do not promise a listing, buyer, transaction, or specific sale price.
Do not price an unvalidated product using only internal cost estimates.
Do not treat technical access controls as substitutes for governance and contracts.

faq.question: What information should I provide first?
faq.answer: Provide the dataset scope, quality, ownership, restrictions, expected buyers, use cases, jurisdiction, costs, and any prior validation.

faq.question: Can this skill determine a final sale price?
faq.answer: It can develop a supported range and negotiation positions. Final pricing requires evidence, buyer feedback, and appropriate professional review.

faq.question: Does this skill provide legal approval?
faq.answer: No. It identifies compliance gates and documentation needs but does not replace qualified legal or regulatory advice.

faq.question: Can it help find buyers?
faq.answer: It can define buyer profiles, matching criteria, outreach preparation, and validation steps. It cannot contact buyers or guarantee interest.

faq.question: When should we consider a trusted data space?
faq.answer: Consider one when participants need controlled computation or analysis without transferring sensitive raw data outside its governed environment.

faq.question: Which AI tools support this skill?
faq.answer: The package declares support for Claude, Codex, and Claude Code.
